Witness: David Chen
Address: 1816 Cedar Street, Apt 2 (next-door neighbor to plaintiff)
Statement taken by: J. Okafor, Esq., 07/02/2024

I was on my front porch on June 7 — I'd guess between 9:00 and 9:30 at night — when I saw Maya walking her dog past my place like she does most evenings. A police car pulled up behind her with no lights or siren. Two officers got out, one male, one female.

The male officer started asking her questions. I couldn't hear all of it but I heard him say something about "complaints." Maya took out her wallet and handed him her ID. He looked at it but didn't give it back. He told her to sit down on the curb. She asked why, and the female officer grabbed her arm — pretty fast, no warning that I saw — and pushed her down on her front. Maya's face hit the sidewalk. I heard her scream.

I started recording on my phone at that point. I have a 1:32 video showing Maya in handcuffs on the ground, the female officer kneeling on her back, the male officer standing. I'll provide a copy.

Maya was on the ground or seated in cuffs for what felt like 40 minutes or more. They eventually uncuffed her and drove off. They never said why they stopped her.

I've lived on this block for 9 years. I've seen MHPD do this kind of stop to Black residents probably a dozen times. I've never seen them do it to a white resident.

Signed: David Chen, 07/02/2024
